atoms.description: Routes to different version-detection logic based on user input: explicit versions, auto-detect, or last two releases.
atoms.evidence: Step 0 table shows all three routing paths: no versions given → auto-detect, explicit versions → skip Step 1, and 'last two releases' → Step 1.

atoms.description: Three git commands to extract most recent and second-most-recent tags for auto-detection: git tag --sort, git describe, and git tag with sed.
atoms.evidence: Step 1 includes all three commands: 'git tag --sort=-version:refname | head -5', 'git describe --tags --abbrev=0', and 'git tag --sort=-version:refname | sed -n '2p''.

atoms.description: When no git tags exist, stop and instruct user to create initial tag with git tag -a command.
atoms.evidence: Step 1 states 'If no tags: stop and show `git tag -a v1.0.0 -m 'Initial release'`.' Error handling table repeats this action.

atoms.description: When only one tag exists, use that tag as OLD and HEAD as NEW.
atoms.evidence: Step 1 specifies: 'If one tag: `$OLD` = that tag, `$NEW` = `HEAD`'.

atoms.description: Four git commands to build complete change catalog: git diff with name-status, git diff with stat, and two git ls-tree commands.
atoms.evidence: Step 2 includes all four commands: 'git diff $OLD $NEW --name-status', 'git diff $OLD $NEW --stat', 'git ls-tree --name-only $OLD', and 'git ls-tree --name-only $NEW'.

atoms.description: Lookup table mapping file path patterns to component keys: skills/, docs/, dashboard/, assets/, and root.
atoms.evidence: Component taxonomy table lists all five mappings: skills/, docs/, dashboard/, assets/, and root with their matching patterns.

atoms.description: Rules for assigning component-level status (NEW, REMOVED, MODIFIED, UNCHANGED) based on file existence and changes.
atoms.evidence: Component-level status explanation provided: NEW (dir didn't exist), REMOVED (gone), MODIFIED (≥1 file changed), UNCHANGED (no files changed), with root-specific rule.

atoms.description: Maps git status codes (A, M, D, R) to file change types (added, modified, deleted, renamed).
atoms.evidence: Per-file catalog section states: 'Git Status (`A`=NEW, `M`=MODIFIED, `D`=REMOVED, `R`=renamed)'.

atoms.description: Commands to extract version field from SKILL.md front matter: git show for OLD version and head for NEW version.
atoms.evidence: Step 3 specifies both commands: 'git show $OLD:skills/<name>/SKILL.md | head -10' for OLD version and 'head -10 skills/<name>/SKILL.md' for NEW version.

atoms.description: When version field is missing from SKILL.md, use 'unknown' in diagrams and tables.
atoms.evidence: Step 3 states: 'No `version:` → use `"unknown"`. Error handling table confirms: 'No `version:` in SKILL.md | Use `"unknown"`'.

atoms.description: When git show fails for a skill file, treat skill as NEW regardless of catalog classification.
atoms.evidence: Step 3 notes: 'If `git show $OLD:...` fails, treat skill as NEW.' Error handling table provides identical rule.

atoms.description: Node IDs must be camelCase only with no hyphens or spaces; map skill names with hyphens to camelCase equivalents.
atoms.evidence: Node structure section states: 'Node IDs: camelCase, no hyphens (e.g. `sdd-orchestrator` → `sddOrchestrator`, `docs/` → `docsNode`)' and formatting rules repeat: 'Node IDs: camelCase, no hyphens, no spaces'.

atoms.description: Node labels must use double quotes and newline character \n for line breaks.
atoms.evidence:
Node structure section specifies: 'Node labels: `"Label
(details)"` — skill nodes: `"sdd-orchestrator
v2.0.0"`, component nodes: `"docs/
3 files changed"'.

atoms.description: Color scheme for Mermaid nodes by status: UNCHANGED (blue-gray), MODIFIED (amber), NEW (green), REMOVED (red) with fill, stroke, and text colors.
atoms.evidence: Style colors table provides all four status rows with fill, stroke, and color values: UNCHANGED (#1e293b/#60a5fa/#e2e8f0), MODIFIED (#1c1507/#f59e0b/#fef3c7), NEW (#052e16/#22c55e/#dcfce7), REMOVED (#1c0707/#f87171/#fee2e2).

atoms.description: OLD diagram includes only components/skills existing at OLD version; excludes NEW items; marks REMOVED items with REMOVED color.
atoms.evidence: OLD diagram section states: 'Include all components/skills that existed at `$OLD`. Exclude NEW items. Mark REMOVED items with REMOVED color'.

atoms.description: NEW diagram includes all components at current state; applies color per component/skill status; separates standalone skills into subgraph.
atoms.evidence: NEW diagram section specifies: 'Include ALL components at current state. Apply color per status. Standalone skills go in a separate subgraph'.

atoms.description: Mermaid formatting requirements: camelCase IDs, double-quoted labels, individual style statements (no classDef), wrap in pre.mermaid tags in HTML.
atoms.evidence: Mermaid formatting rules section lists all requirements: camelCase IDs, double-quoted labels, individual style statements (no classDef), and wrap in `<pre class="mermaid">` with escaped `<`/`>` characters.

atoms.description: All template placeholders with their sources: OLD_VERSION, NEW_VERSION, GENERATED_DATE, OLD_DIAGRAM, NEW_DIAGRAM, skill counts, step counts, and file change counts.
atoms.evidence: Step 5 placeholder table documents all variables with sources: OLD_VERSION, NEW_VERSION, GENERATED_DATE, diagram placeholders, skill/step counts, file change counts, and UNCHANGED_COUNT.

atoms.description: HTML table row format for changed files: component group headers, file name, badge status, version columns, and notes; sorted by component.
atoms.evidence: Step 5 change table specification describes row format: path | badge status | version columns | notes, with component group headers and badge classes (badge-new, badge-modified, badge-removed).

atoms.description: Change table rows must be grouped by component in order: skills/, docs/, dashboard/, assets/, root files; with group-header separator rows.
atoms.evidence: Step 5 states: 'Sort: `skills/` → `docs/` → `dashboard/` → `assets/` → root. Add `<tr class="group-header">` before each group'.

atoms.description: Badge CSS classes by git status: badge-new (A), badge-modified (M), badge-removed (D).
atoms.evidence: Change table section specifies: 'Badge class: `badge-new` (A) | `badge-modified` (M) | `badge-removed` (D)'.

atoms.description: Version columns populate only for skill SKILL.md files; all other files use '—' as placeholder.
atoms.evidence: Change table section states: 'Version columns only for SKILL.md files; others use `—`'.

atoms.description: Output HTML file path: assets/diff-VERSION1-to-VERSION2.html; use HEAD if NEW is HEAD.
atoms.evidence: Step 6 specifies: 'Write to: `assets/diff-$OLD-to-$NEW.html` (HEAD variant: `assets/diff-vX.Y.Z-to-HEAD.html`)'.

atoms.description: Requires template file at references/html-template.md; must be read and placeholders replaced before writing output.
atoms.evidence: Step 6 requires: 'Read template from `references/html-template.md`'. References section confirms: 'HTML template: `references/html-template.md`'.

atoms.description: HTML file must be self-contained with no local file references; only CDN links allowed.
atoms.evidence: Step 6 states: 'Self-contained — CDN links only, no local file references'.

atoms.description: When template file is missing, stop and report error with expected path.
atoms.evidence: Error handling table states: 'Template missing | Stop. Report path and suggest reinstalling skill'.

atoms.description: When no files differ between versions, report and stop.
atoms.evidence: Error handling table specifies: 'No files changed | Report: "No differences found between $OLD and $NEW."'.

atoms.description: When Mermaid text exceeds ~4000 characters, split into two sub-diagrams stacked vertically.
atoms.evidence: Error handling table includes: 'Mermaid text > ~4000 chars | Split into two sub-diagrams stacked vertically'.

atoms.description: Before writing file, verify no remaining {{...}} tokens and no unescaped <> characters in node labels.
atoms.evidence: Step 6 includes verification: 'Verify no remaining `{{...}}` tokens'.

atoms.description: User-facing report structure: file path, change summary counts, component status list, and optional next steps.
atoms.evidence: Step 7 provides user report structure: 'Report output path, change summary (added/modified/removed counts per component), and that it opens in any browser without a server.'
